title: Allocation Concealment versus Variance in History-Dependent Restricted Randomization
banked_reason: Field-level novelty remains unsupported until theorem-level Grant--Anstrom and original maximal-procedure text can be compared assumption by assumption; the mathematical separation was not refuted.
gap_reasons: Field-level novelty remains unsupported until theorem-level text for GrantAnstrom2008 and the original maximal-procedure analysis is compared assumption by assumption with the common-cap, full-history-versus-time/imbalance target.
proof_attempt_summary: Three proposal/review passes repaired the construction language, credited the maximal-procedure and Grant--Anstrom precedents, and narrowed the claim to a common spectral-covariance-cap separation that persists for all even cohort sizes and asymptotically. The reviewers found no soundness defect and no inspected theorem subsuming that conjunction, but repeated the same novelty objection because the decisive Grant--Anstrom section and original maximal-procedure theorem text were inaccessible. Re-raise only after obtaining those primary texts and completing an equation-by-equation assumption comparison; the exact witness and composition mathematics remain reusable.
tldr: Can retaining a finite amount of allocation history reduce predictable selection beyond every time-and-current-imbalance rule, while preserving exact terminal balance, width-two prefixes, global label symmetry, and the same full-covariance cap? The proposed answer is an explicit full-support controller family at cap \(3/2\), with a strictly positive finite-size and asymptotic susceptibility gap. The covariance cap gives an exact worst-case variance safeguard for a fixed cohort; the prediction score concerns possible adaptive enrollment and is a separate diagnostic.
gap: Berger2005 already gives the full-support terminal-balanced width-two maximal procedure inside the comparator class, and GrantAnstrom2008 supplies nonuniform finite selection-game precedent. The provisional gap is a positive universal full-history advantage under one whole-covariance cap for both classes, at every even size and asymptotically. Grant–Anstrom §7 full text is the remaining priority limit.
fill: Prove the exact seed and filler certificates, covariance-preserving odd join, explicit bounded-state controller realization, and universal precision lower bound for all time-varying imbalance-only laws.
